A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SPORT study. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison support matching the methods, equations, tables, figures, and complete Appendices A–H. v5 adds a checklist without removing scientific material.

before.justification: v4 reports original GTA and GAIA evaluations, ablations, human evaluations of generated tasks and preferences, and computational-efficiency analyses.

after.justification: v5 retains these original empirical results, including benchmark scores in Table 1, human evaluations in Tables 7 and 10, and repeated-run results in Table 11.

M1.justification: SPORT's task synthesis, alternating step sampling and verification, preference-pair construction, and DPO tuning remain unchanged. Section 3, Algorithm 1, and the appendix prompts describe the same procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic multimodal tasks, GTA and GAIA benchmarks, task-generation evaluations, and human-study scenarios. The checklist introduces no additional evaluated domain or task.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same Lego, Warm-up, HF, and T3-Agent comparisons. The static-DPO, verifier, and task-generation comparator sets also remain unchanged. The newly cited GUI-agent work is not added to an experimental comparison.

E3.justification: Training settings, evaluation metrics, inference procedures, ablation configurations, and human-study sample sizes and tasks are unchanged. The checklist's ethics-review and consent statements disclose information about existing studies rather than establish a revised experimental design.

E4.justification: The iteration-size, static-preference, base-model, and task-diversity ablations are retained unchanged, as are preference-data analyses, computational-efficiency analysis, and qualitative cases in the main text and appendices.

E5.justification: Appendix E already reports five repetitions and performance variance in v4. v5 retains the same text and Table 11 uncertainty entries; the checklist merely points to this existing reporting.

E6.justification: Table 1 retains SPORT's 60.26% GTA and 20.61% GAIA answer accuracies. All other numerical results, including ablations, human ratings, compute estimates, and uncertainty values, are unchanged, as are the qualitative findings.

T1.justification: The agent formulation, preference-data definitions, and DPO objective in Equations 1–3 remain unchanged. Neither version contains additional theoretical results or proofs; the checklist's theory answer introduces no mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about autonomous tool-use exploration, step-wise preference tuning, benchmark improvements, and the 16K preference dataset. The checklist affirms rather than revises these contributions.

C2.justification: Checklist item 11 newly argues that controlled tool interaction presents minimal risk and requires no additional safeguards beyond standard responsible use. This adds a risk assessment; the verifier limitations in Section 5 and broader deployment concerns in Appendix A remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The checklist newly states that code, the data-generation pipeline, and preference data are supplied as supplemental material, and promises public release after the decision. It also reports ethics review and informed consent. Existing implementation details and the project link remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish an actual change in external resource availability.

R1.justification: v5 adds Li et al., Efficient Multi-Turn RL for GUI Agents via Decoupled Training and Adaptive Data Curation, as reference 30 and cites it in the introduction. Existing references are retained, with subsequent numbering shifted; SPORT's substantive positioning is unchanged.

P1.justification: v5 inserts a standalone NeurIPS checklist containing answers and template guidance, adds affiliation 5 for Zhi Gao, and expands the funding acknowledgements. Existing scientific prose and the relative order of its sections are retained without extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: The checklist introduces a new document block before the appendices, while acknowledgements and references reflow. Figures 1–18 and Tables 1–11 retain their designs and positions within corresponding sections; appendix pagination shifts without restructuring those displays.

improvement.justification: The new checklist modestly improves reporting transparency by explicitly documenting ethics review and informed consent and describing code/data provision. The scientific evidence is unchanged. Much of the checklist repeats existing material and retains template instructions, while actual resource availability is not established by the PDFs, limiting the overall benefit.
